title: Avatar-assisted medication administration with AI-based intake monitoring - Usability testing and testing in participants' homes (Module B and C)
summary:
The regular and correct use of prescribed medication is essential for older adults and individuals with chronic conditions to prevent health complications and reduce disease progression. Nevertheless, numerous challenges can impede medication adherence, including forgetfulness, difficulties in understanding medication instructions, and uncertainty regarding medication management. As a result, a considerable proportion of patients do not take their medications as prescribed. Digital technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), offer promising opportunities to support medication adherence through personalized reminders, motivational communication, and automated verification of medication intake.

Building on the findings from Module A—a qualitative interview study exploring experiences, perceptions, needs, and the acceptance of a digital AI-supported solution for medication management and adherence monitoring—a demonstrator (i.e., a prototype) was developed. This medication assistant incorporates the functional and design requirements identified during the initial study phase. The focus of the second phase of the project (Modules B and C) is the systematic evaluation of this medication assistant across different usage contexts in order to investigate user experiences, acceptance, and opportunities for further refinement and development.
conditions: Medication adherence, older adults, digital health, medication management, assistive system

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For Module B:
•    Setting: either community-dwelling or geriatric patients receiving outpatient care
•    Medication: Long-term therapy (≥ 3 months) involving ≥ 5 prescription medications (tablets/capsules)
•    Autonomy in medication administration: Patients take their medication independently, without regular assistance from nursing staff or family members
•    Data collection: Consent to audio recording
•    Concurrent participation: No participation in “AvatarMediKI – Avatar-assisted medication administration with AI-based intake monitoring – Perspectives and challenges (Module A)” or home-based testing (Module C)

For Module C:
•    Setting: either living independently (community-dwelling) or geriatric patients receiving outpatient care
•    Medication: Long-term therapy ≥ 3 months with ≥5 prescription medications (tablets/capsules)
•    Autonomy in medication intake: Taking medication independently, without regular support from nursing staff or relatives
•    Data collection: Consent to audio recording
•    Technology in the home: Consent to the installation of the demonstrator in the living environment
•    Internet: Consent to the setup/use of internet access (existing or available)
•    Concurrent participation: No participation in the interview study “AvatarMediKI – Avatar-assisted medication administration with AI-based intake monitoring – Perspectives and challenges” (Modules A/B)
Exclusion criteria:
For Modules B and C:
•    Capacity to consent and reflect: dementia, acute delirium, or a comparable impairment of the capacity to consent and reflect
